title: Seller ops velocity playlet + annotations (draft)
body:
Purpose
- Short annotated playlet for sellers to run a 30–90 minute pilot handoff with platform/ops. Focus on velocity: reduce time-to-first-successful-API-call and minimize follow-up work for SRE/Platform.

TL;DR (1-line)
- Run the three-stage playlet: QuickQual -> TechHandshake -> CanaryKickoff. Use the script fragments below, note the annotated operator cues, and prefer the fast-fallback options if latency or reliability signals appear.

Audience
- Primary: SEs and sellers working mid-market/platform accounts. Secondary: platform engineers who will receive the pilot.

When to use this doc
- Customer is interested in a short pilot and asks "how fast can we be live?"
- They have non-trivial latency constraints or strict reliability needs
- You expect routing/pinning or private deploy requirements within the pilot window

High-level constraints to call out on the first call
- Latency target: customer SLO (e.g., 200–500ms p95 for short completions). Call out sequence length expectations.
- Data residency: any need for private or VPC? If yes, skip hosted-only pilot.
- Throughput shape: bursty vs steady; estimate RPS and concurrency.
- Failure tolerance: will they accept lower-quality fallbacks during outages? If no, plan a dedicated small pool.

Playlet overview (3 stages)
1) QuickQual (10–15m) — goal: confirm API basics and fatal constraints
  - Script snippets for seller: "For an initial pilot we typically validate 3 things in 30 minutes: a) API auth and test call b) one representative prompt scenario c) a latency/throughput sketch. Are you able to provision a single engineer for short call?"
  - Operator cue: ask for a sample prompt and expected tokens. Collect sequence length distribution (e.g., avg 40 tokens, 99p 400).
  - Quick accept criteria: auth works, sample prompt completes, and customer agrees to run a short canary.

2) TechHandshake (20–40m) — goal: align infra choices + fallback policy
  - Topics to cover (annotated):
    - Model choice: prefer a smaller compatible variant for initial canary (e.g., redwood-small/quant) to reduce latency/cost. Note: if customer demands parity with production model, plan dedicated capacity.
    - Routing policy: single-region or multi-region? If multi-region, enumerate endpoint hosts and estimate cross-region latency penalty.
    - Caching & prefixes: identify reusable prefixes (instruction prompt) for KV/prefix caching to lower per-token cost — ask for normalized prompt examples.
    - Fallback plan (must be explicit): degrade to cheaper model variant vs queue requests vs return informative error. Mark customer's preference.
  - Sample handshake script: "If we see p95 latency exceed 700ms in the canary, we should fall back to redwood-small. Is that acceptable? If not, we will scope a 24–48h dedicated capacity request."
  - Operator cue: create a minimal ticket (JIRA-1254 style) for any infra changes. Capture owner and ETA.

3) CanaryKickoff (30–90m) — goal: run an instrumented end-to-end test with observable SLIs
  - Steps (annotated):
    a) Provision API key + route; confirm simple test call from customer network (10m)
    b) Run 50–100 representative calls using customer samples (can be scripted, 10–30m)
    c) Observe latency, error rate, token cost; collect 1-minute metrics and p95/p99 (30–60m)
  - Live checklist (for SE):
    - Confirm ingestion logs, request ids (traceable)
    - Confirm model variant and quantization profile used
    - Confirm fallback occurred (if triggered) and that it matched agreement
  - Quick exit criteria: pilot meets customer SLOs or fallback behavior accepted by customer.

Annotated seller scripts (short)
- Opening micro-pitch (10s): "We prioritize getting a signal fast — with a tiny canary we can validate latency, quality signal, and routing policy in under 90 minutes."
- If they push for immediate production parity: "We can run parity but it often adds 1–2 days for capacity and checks — can we confirm parity needs now or start with a fast canary and iterate?"
- Objection: "We need SLA." Reply: "For a full SLA-backed environment we scope Dedicated capacity — this pilot validates functional fit and performance envelope so we can size that commitment."

Decision heuristics matrix (text)
- If p95 latency < customer SLO on small variant -> propose scaled pilot on the same variant; recommend batching + prefix caching to lower cost.
- If p95 latency borderline but quality OK -> route to quota-limited dedicated burst or increase parallelism on dedicated lanes.
- If quality drop on small variant -> escalate to model-parity pilot (dedicated capacity), log as quality-regression.

Sample acceptance rubric (pass/fail notes)
- Pass if: auth/test call success, p95 latency <= SLO, error rate < 1%, customer confirms sample output quality >= baseline.
- Fail if: repeated 5xx errors, p99 latency > 2x SLO, unacceptable hallucination rate on sample prompts.

Operational notes for SRE handoff (bullet list)
- Tag ticket with pilot id and include: sample prompts, expected traffic shape, chosen fallback, contact on call.
- Pre-create a rollback plan: route traffic to fallback variant + disable automatic retries.
- Keep a 2-hour monitoring window after enabling canary and schedule a 30-min sync at the 60-minute mark.

Common friction patterns (notes to seller)
- Customer expects full data isolation but wants fastest time-to-value — call out tradeoff: private deployments introduce 2–7 day setup.
- Network egress or firewalling issues: ask for IP allowlist early.
- Billing/legal hold ups: surface early, ask procurement for a short trial agreement or attach existing ALPHA CLA.

Playlet variations (quick list)
- Quick API-only: skip dedicated infra discussion, run only QuickQual + CanaryKickoff (45–60m).
- Compliance-first: insert privacy & KMS check between QuickQual and TechHandshake, likely extends timeline to days.
- Integrator mode: add 30m for SDK + sample integration (webhook, function-calls) in TechHandshake.

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- Confirm if we should include a prebuilt Postman collection for the canary (PR open: platform-prs#482).
- Need standard phrasing for fallback economic impact (tokens & $) for sellers to quote.
- Decide whether to surface a binary "dedicated needed" checkbox in pilot intake form.

Next steps (owner: Priya)
- Finalize Postman collection and place in shared kit (due: 2026-03-01)
- Draft short internal one-pager for Finance on pilot billing estimates (due: 2026-02-28)
- Run an internal dry-run with Solutions Eng this week; capture timing deviations.

Notes to self (shorthand)
- keep the scripts short, 2 lines max ideally.
- add a tiny appendix later: example curl + sample output and JSON keys to search for in logs.
- ping SE pod in #g2m-se for refinements after 3rd pilot.

Appendix (links & quick artifacts)
- Example curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-small","prompt":"<example>"}'
- Confluence note: ops-velocity-reference (see linked artifacts)

End of draft.

(Informal tone, intentionally concise for seller-readability; will expand examples and add curl/postman samples in next iteration)
